title: Load the night's meter readings in chunks

blocks.text: Every night the utility imports its smart-meter readings, about 2.4 million rows, into a database on another host. `importOneByOne` in `src/main/java/practice/MeterImport.java` does the job correctly, but the import now runs past the start of the morning shift, and the DBA reports that it sends a different SQL text for every reading. Meter names come from the vendor's file unchanged, and some contain quotes.

Write `importAll(connection, readings, chunkSize)` so the import reaches the driver once per `chunkSize` readings rather than once per reading, sends the database one SQL text for the whole run, and returns the number of rows the database reports inserted. The connection is the caller's: don't close it or commit. About twelve lines.

headers: calls that send rows to the database

blocks.text: The table is `meter_reading(meter VARCHAR(40), wh BIGINT)`.

cases.says: every reading is stored and the method returns the number of rows inserted
an empty list stores nothing and returns 0
30 readings in chunks of 10 reach the driver in three executeBatch calls and no executeUpdate
one SQL text with placeholders is prepared for the whole import; no reading's value is part of any SQL text, and names with quotes are stored as they are
11 readings in chunks of 4 are all stored, the last three included

origin.section: A PreparedStatement Is Parsed Once and Bound Per Row; a Batch Sends the Rows in One Call

concepts: A PreparedStatement is parsed once and executed with new bound values; addBatch/executeBatch sends many rows in one call into the driver instead of one call per row.
Bound values never become part of the SQL text, so the statement text is the same for every row and a value with quotes can't change it.
